what_its_for: Thioridazine is used to treat schizophrenia. It helps reduce symptoms such as hallucinations (hearing or seeing things that are not there), delusions (false beliefs), and disorganized thinking. It is usually used when other medications have not worked well enough.
how_to_take: Take thioridazine exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help if it upsets your stomach. Try to take it at the same times each day. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and how your body responds to the medicine. Doses are usually taken 2 to 4 times per day. Never take more or less than your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store thioridazine at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep it away from the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do activities that require you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine can cause dizziness. Stay out of extreme heat and stay well hydrated, as this medicine can affect your body's ability to cool down. Avoid taking antacids or other medicines within 2 hours of thioridazine without asking your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: uncontrolled muscle movements in your face, tongue, or body (such as twitching or jerking); a fast, irregular, or pounding heartbeat or chest pain; fainting or severe dizziness; high fever, stiff muscles, confusion, or sweating (these could be signs of a rare but serious condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome); trouble swallowing or breathing; seizures; vision changes; painful or prolonged erection (men); yellowing of the skin or eyes; or signs of infection such as fever or sore throat. Also contact your doctor if you feel more depressed or have thoughts of harming yourself.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice some improvement in your symptoms within a few days to a few weeks, but it may take several weeks to feel the full benefit of this medicine. It is important to keep taking it even if you do not feel better right away. Talk to your doctor if you do not notice any improvement after several weeks.
special_populations: Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness, confusion, and falls. Thioridazine is generally not recommended for elderly patients with dementia-related behavior problems due to an increased risk of serious events including death. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine may not be safe during pregnancy, and it may pass into breast milk. Children: This medicine may be used in children 2 years and older in specific situations, but only under close doctor supervision. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
